summary: A cast-iron spark-plug tower rising from open water beside the Ambrose Channel, lit in 1901, raised in 1908 and now privately owned.

access.note: Privately owned; tower closed; offshore, best seen from a boat.

events.note: Fixed white fourth-order light with red sector; report text says 1 Jan 1901, its list gives 31 Jan 1901
Struck by Carrie Winslow in tow, 28 Dec 1904
Raised by two stories, finished 8 Jan 1908
Barge No. 19 in tow struck the tower
Declared excess by the Coast Guard, May 2007
Sold at second GSA auction for $195,000

notes_for_editor: Nomination PDF (06001230) not digitised, so NRHP text was not read. Dates of raising (8 Jan 1908), Carrie Winslow and 1915 barge collisions, post-war Coast Guard life, auctions and Reilly's plan rest on LighthouseFriends (copyrighted; paraphrased) because the 1902-1910 Light-House Board volumes are not in the corpus and newspaper search found nothing. Burdge quotes are from Fullerton, American Magazine June 1920, as quoted there. LF says tower raised to 70 ft; USLHS gives 55 ft base to lantern centre, 69 ft focal height; not reconciled. Staten Island rear light: 15 April 1912 (Commissioner 1915) vs 5 April (LF). LF reads the 1901 report as 1,528 tons riprap; OCR gives 1,628, so tonnage omitted. Name variants: Gundersen/Gunderson, Nielsen/Nielson, Kjelberg. Wikipedia gives automation 1985, LF early 1980s. 1918/1919 Bulletin rescue dates (Penn/Stryker Nov 1918; McCoart Apr 1919) inferred from roster spans; Bulletin OCR is poor. Current ownership unverified after 2013 (LF says Reilly meant to donate to the Romer Shoal group). Fact-check 2026-10-22: Bulletin 1919 gives the Penn/Stryker rescue as 'November 10' without a year in the OCR; 1918 inferred from Penn's roster span (story says so). Burdge quotations: LF's reference list names Fullerton, American Magazine June 1920, but LF itself calls one interview 1924, so per-quote attribution is left unstated. Private buyer not named in the story (living-people rule); LF names him. 1901 report text says blower siren, its list says compressed-air siren (both now stated).
